newsitem.title: USA: Conseco acquisitions to sharpen its focus.
newsitem.headline: Conseco acquisitions to sharpen its focus.

text.p: Conseco Inc's $2.04 billion four-pronged acquisition plan disclosed Monday will sharpen the Carmel, Ind.-financial services company's focus on insurance segments serving the nation's aging population.
"After the transactions are completed, we will have a number one position in long-term care (insurance)," chairman Stephen Hilbert told reporters in a teleconference.

In universal life, Conseco will have a number two position after State Farm Insurance, and Hilbert said "Our goal is to have the number one market share in universal life over the next 18 to 24 months."

The multiple transaction also will place Conseco among the top five companies writing retirement savings annuities. "We're going to be producing at about $2 billion a year of new first-year annuity premiums," Hilbert said.

Conseco agreed to buy American Travellers Corp, a provider of long-term care insurance, Capitol American Financial Corp, which provides cancer insurance and other supplemental health insurance products.
It also plans to buy shares not already held of American Life Holdings and the balance of Bankers Life Holdings Corp.
Hilbert said Conseco expects to realize savings of $30 million to $32 million from the transactions, which are expected to be completed by the fourth quarter.
Savings will come primarily by consolidating data processing, investment management and other financial functions, including actuarial.
American Life Holdings operations will move to Conseco's Carmel, Ind. headquarters from Des Moines. However, Hilbert said it was too early to gauge the extent of any staff cutbacks.

Chief financial officer Rollin Dick reiterated that the effect of the acquisitions would be to add about $0.35 per share to 1997 earnings, enabling the company to reach its earnings goal of $5 per fully diluted share next year.
Dick also noted that rating agencies have responded favorably to Conseco's acquisition plans.
Because of Conseco's active acquisition efforts -- it added 25 insurance companies to its fold since February 1992 -- Hilbert said there was a misperception about its growth strategy.

"Dig through the numbers and you'll find 60 percent of our growth has come from how we have taken those companies, created a better product line and broadened their distribution for internal growth," Hilbert said. "Looking forward, you'll see internal growth go from 60 percent to 70 to 75 percent." Externally, the company should grow by about 25 percent.
"We are going to be looking at future transactions, but we're going to be very selective," Hilbert said.
He added that any future acquisitions would be structured to maintain Conseco's targeted debt-to-capital ratio in the 30 to 35 percent range.
Analyst Seth Potter of Sands Brothers & Co said the acquisitions "will give Conseco a lot of muscle, especially in long-term care."
Frederick Sandburg of EVEREN Securities Inc said as the 45-to-60-age continues to mature, demand for insurance in this segment will steadily rise.
